profile.summary: A spreading New Zealand conifer shrub of mountain scrub, tussock grassland and rocky alpine ground. Its branches often form a low, dense dome.
profile.lookFor: Small, closely spaced stiff leaves on densely leafy twigs; green seeds sit above swollen red receptacles.
profile.nameNote: Flora of New Zealand lists Tauhinu for Podocarpus nivalis. Tauhinu is shared with other shrubs; mountain tōtara and snow tōtara are also documented common names, and tōtara occurs in the names of several Podocarpus species.

profile.summary: An endemic bushy shrub or small tree of coastal and lowland forest. It has small firm leaves, white flowers and red to dark berries.
profile.lookFor: Opposite leaves with a clear notch at the tip, giving a reversed heart shape; white flowers have many stamens.

profile.summary: A much-branched New Zealand conifer shrub or small tree with different juvenile and adult foliage. Some spreading branches root where they touch the ground.
profile.lookFor: Adult twigs have tiny overlapping scale leaves; dark grooved seeds are held in conspicuous waxy white cups.

profile.summary: A common native small tree in coastal, lowland and lower mountain forests. Its pale bark and toothed leaves are useful recognition features.
profile.lookFor: Light green tapered leaves with toothed edges; tiny flowers cluster along twigs and berries ripen purple.
profile.nameNote: The NZPCN factsheet uses Melicytus ramiflorus subsp. ramiflorus for the New Zealand taxon and discusses the treatment of former Pacific subspecies. The WRT species-level name is retained.
